info.title: AKIRA Ops Suite API
info.description:
Internal multi-outlet restaurant operations platform.

Authenticate with a Supabase access token: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

get.description:
Profile, global role and outlet memberships for the current session.

The client uses this to decide which shell to render, so it is the first
call after sign-in.

patch.description:
Change your own name or phone. Role, outlets and activation are not
editable here — those are administrative actions.

get.description:
What the signed-in user may grant, plus a plain-language reason for each
role they may not. The UI disables the rest with the reason attached rather
than omitting them — a rule you cannot see is a rule you will argue with.

Owners and operations managers see everyone. An outlet manager sees only
people in their own outlets.

post.description:
Supabase sends the invitation and owns the token, so no password is ever
handled here.

You can never grant a role at or above your own. An existing address is not
an error: that person keeps the login they already have.

patch.description:
Deactivating the last active owner is refused: it would lock everyone out
of outlet and user administration permanently.

put.description: Outlet roles follow the global role, so the two cannot silently disagree.
Replaces the whole set. The first outlet becomes their primary.

put.summary: Set or clear a shared-tablet PIN
put.description:
A PIN attributes floor work on a shared tablet to a real person. It
authorises floor actions only, can never approve a run, and is only accepted
on a device already bound to that person's outlet.

Sending `null` clears it, which is how a departing staff member comes off
the tablet without losing their history. Only shift leads and staff may
have one.

get.description:
Owners and operations managers see every outlet. Everyone else sees only
the outlets they belong to.

schema.description: Include outlets that have been deactivated.
schema.title: Include Inactive

parameters.description: Include outlets that have been deactivated.

post.description: Owner only. The code must be unique and is fixed once created.

patch.description:
Owner only. Changes only the fields present in the body. The code cannot
be changed — it appears in exports and printed sheets.

delete.description:
Owner only. A soft delete: history is kept, the outlet stops appearing.

Refused with 409 while any checklist run is still pending, in progress or
awaiting review — closing the outlet under them would strand work someone
is in the middle of.

post.description:
Owner only. Binds an existing Supabase auth account to one outlet.

The account itself is created out of band, so this API never mints or
transports a credential.

delete.description:
Owner only. Use this the moment a tablet goes missing: it stops that
account reaching any outlet data, without touching the runs it already
recorded.

Inserts a new effective-dated row rather than editing the old one, so
scoring a past period keeps using the values that were live then.

Scoring weights and bands are owner-only; the operational groups
(integrity, AI review, jobs) accept an operations manager too.

get.description:
Newest first. A gap where a scheduled job should have run is as
significant as a failure row — both mean the job did not do its work.

post.summary: Run a scheduled job now (owner only)
post.description:
Owner only, and every one of these is safe to press twice.

Materialisation is idempotent by unique constraint; marking missed only
moves runs already past grace; the digest re-sends a report rather than
changing anything. Nothing here is destructive, which is why it can be a
button at all — but it does send mail, so it is not left to ops managers.

schema.title: Response Outlet Health Dashboard Outlet Health Get

post.description:
Accepts a Petpooja .xlsx export and parses it in the background.

Two reports are understood, told apart by their header row: the Orders
Master Report (bills) and the Order Listing report (item names per bill).
The uploader does not choose — the file says what it is, and anything
else is refused here in the request.

The outlet is chosen here rather than read from the file: a Petpooja export
names only the restaurant, so two outlets produce indistinguishable files.

Re-sending a file already ingested returns the original upload untouched —
idempotency is on the bytes, not the filename, which carries an export
timestamp and changes every time.

schema.title: Response Upload Export Sales Uploads Post

get.description:
Newest first, each carrying its warnings. A parser that dropped rows
silently would be a parser nobody could trust, so what it skipped travels
with the upload.

schema.title: Response List Uploads Sales Uploads Get

post.description:
Re-read the stored original — after an adapter version bump, or after
fixing whatever made it fail. The file is kept precisely so nobody has to
go back to Petpooja and export it again.

schema.title: Response Reparse Sales Uploads  Upload Id  Reparse Post

get.description:
Grouped and filtered by `business_date`, never by the calendar date —
a bill at 00:45 belongs to the night before.

schema.title: Response List Orders Sales Orders Get

get.description:
What the Stage 2 sales pillar will read. Here now because it is the
cheapest way to see whether an ingest landed on the days it should.

get.summary: How often each item appears on a bill
get.description:
Appearances, not units: the Order Listing carries names without
quantities, so a bill with two Shoyu Ramen counts once. Empty until a
listing has been uploaded for the outlet.

Scoped by role: staff see staff runs, shift leads see floor runs,
managers see everything at the outlet. 'Today' is the business date —
at 1am this still returns the evening's checklists.

get.summary: Reference standards for an outlet, including the ones not captured yet
get.description:
Every photo-requiring item, with its standard attached if one exists.

Listing the gaps is the whole job. A screen that showed only what has been
captured would make an outlet with two standards look finished.

post.description:
Confirms the object exists, retires the previous standard, and records
the new one. The luminance measurement runs afterwards: a standard shot in
a dark room would make every honest submission look bright by comparison,
so the number is captured for the same reason submissions are measured.

patch.description:
Name, category, frequency, day part, active flag. None of these bumps
the version — only item changes are material.

post.description: A fresh version-1 copy, inactive and unassigned, ready to edit.
Bumps the template version and snapshots every item, in one transaction.

patch.description:
Every field here is material: the edit bumps the version, and runs
recorded before it keep rendering the old definition.

delete.description:
Hard delete only if no run has ever answered against it; otherwise a
soft delete that keeps history renderable.

put.description:
Takes every current item id in the new order. Partial lists are refused
rather than silently dropping the forgotten items.

schema.title: Response List Assignments Sop Assignments Get

post.summary: Assign a template to an outlet

delete.description:
Soft delete. Runs already materialised from it are untouched; no new
ones are created.

get.summary: Who can identify on this tablet
get.description:
The PIN-pad picker: floor staff of the tablet's outlet. Only meaningful
on a device session; an individual login is already somebody.

schema.title: Response List Floor Staff Floor Staff Get

post.description:
Turns a device session plus a correct PIN into a short-lived actor
assertion. Five wrong attempts lock the PIN for five minutes. Every
failure is audited.

The assertion authorises floor actions only. It can never approve a run
and never reaches the management shell.

get.description: Liveness probe. Must never touch the database.

Readiness probe. Unlike /healthz this does check the database, because a
process that cannot reach Postgres is running but not serving.

DeviceSummary.title: DeviceSummary
DeviceSummary.description: Present only when the caller is a shared outlet tablet.

GrantableRolesResponse.title: GrantableRolesResponse
GrantableRolesResponse.description:
What the signed-in user may assign, so the UI can disable the rest with
an explanation instead of hiding it.

SetOutletsRequest.title: SetOutletsRequest
SetOutletsRequest.description:
Replaces the whole membership set, rather than adding to it.

A replace makes the resulting state obvious from the request. An add/remove
pair leaves the caller guessing what the person ended up with.

SettingView.title: SettingView
SettingView.description: One setting as the admin screen shows it: definition plus current value.

UpdateMeRequest.title: UpdateMeRequest
UpdateMeRequest.description:
Only what a person may change about themselves.

Role, outlets and activation are deliberately absent: allowing them here
would let anyone promote themselves through their own profile.

UpdateOutletRequest.title: UpdateOutletRequest
UpdateOutletRequest.description:
Every field optional: a PATCH changes only what it names.

`code` is absent on purpose. It appears in exports, conversation and
printed sheets, so renaming it silently would break references nobody is
tracking.

UpdateTemplateItemRequest.title: UpdateTemplateItemRequest
UpdateTemplateItemRequest.description:
Partial edit. Every field here is material (D11): changing any of them
bumps the template version so history keeps rendering what was true.

UpdateTemplateRequest.title: UpdateTemplateRequest
UpdateTemplateRequest.description:
Template-level fields only. None of these is a material change, so none
bumps the version — the items are the contract with history, not the
label on the folder.

UserListItem.title: UserListItem
UserListItem.description: A person as they appear in the admin table.
